title: Unknown phenomena are found only by systematic, preconception-free experiments

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Unknown phenomena are found only by systematic, preconception-free experiments

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Phenomena not already known to exist can be found only by very systematic and general experiments whose results are examined with as few preconceptions as possible.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the only way to find phenomena that one does not already know exist is to do very systematic and general experiments, and then to look at the results with as few preconceptions as possible.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “Why These Discoveries Were Not Made Before” (from p. 42), p. 45. Scope: scientific methodology, especially computer experiments

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-14: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.08

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is primarily a methodological maxim with self-referential and counterfactual content. Existing historical evidence cannot distinguish necessity from one useful discovery strategy across all possible unknown phenomena.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The universal only-way statement lacks a measurable population of all unknown phenomena and all discovery methods. Historical counterexamples might refute a narrow reading, but no finite analysis can confirm the methodological necessity as stated.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Discovery histories are selectively documented.

Systematic, general, and few preconceptions lack objective thresholds.

Unknown phenomena cannot be sampled before discovery.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a norm for inquiry. Histories of discovery can be told so that they fit the norm or so that they do not, because the key terms are not tied to recordable variables. No public dataset decides it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim states that the only way to find genuinely unknown phenomena is systematic, preconception-free experiment. A historical case of serendipity or of a theory-led discovery would bear on the wording only after 'unknown' and 'preconception' are given definitions the sentence does not supply.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Preconception-free observation is not an achievable or recordable condition.

The only way is a methodological absolute, not a measurable regularity.
